WebRoot/auth/admin/addER.jsp: As an administrator using this system, you would: Insert the first name, last name, and email address of the new Emergency Responder into the fields provided on the form. Once you submit the form, the system will create a new account for the Emergency Responder and assign them a unique ID known as the Medical ID (MID). The system shall also generate a temporary password for the new Emergency Responder which you will see after a successful submission. It is your responsibility to convey this important information – the MID and temporary password – to the new Emergency Responder. After seeing the confirmation message, there is an option to proceed to manage further personnel information through an available link. The process is designed to ensure the secure addition of new personnel while maintaining the confidentiality of sensitive information like passwords.

WebRoot/auth/admin/addHCP.jsp:
As an administrator using this system, you would:
Enter the healthcare provider's (HCP) first name, last name, and email address to register them in the database.
After you submit the form, the system will automatically generate a unique Medical ID (MID) for the new HCP.
The system will also generate a temporary password that you will need to provide to the new HCP for login purposes.
The successful addition of the HCP will be confirmed with a message displaying the HCP's MID and temporary password.
From there, you can continue to manage the new HCP's information or update their details in other sections of the system.
This process allows you to efficiently add new healthcare providers to the system while ensuring their credentials are securely initialized.

WebRoot/auth/admin/addPHA.jsp: As an administrator using this system, you would: Enter the new Public Health Administrator's first name, last name, and email address into the form provided. After submitting the form, the system will create a new record for the administrator and generate a unique employee identifier, known as a Medical ID (MID), for them. Along with the MID, a temporary password will also be generated. This information should be communicated to the new administrator so that they can access their account and reset their password. A message confirming the successful addition and the relevant details will be displayed. This process ensures that new Public Health Administrators are added efficiently, with secure access credentials established upon entry into the system.

WebRoot/auth/admin/editApptType.jsp:
As an administrator using this system, you would perform the following actions to manage appointment types within the healthcare scheduling platform: 

Open the interface, which displays a list of current appointment types with their respective names and durations. 

To add a new appointment type, enter the name and expected duration in the provided fields and submit the information using the 'Add Type' option. 

To modify an existing appointment type, select its name from the list—this will populate the fields with its current details—update the information accordingly, then confirm the changes using the 'Update Type' option. 

The system validates the input, displaying any necessary error messages for missing or incorrect information. This ensures all appointment types are correctly configured to match the clinic's scheduling requirements.

WebRoot/auth/admin/editCPTProcedureCodes: As an administrator using this system, you have the ability to manage Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes, which are used for billing and healthcare documentation. You can add new CPT codes with their respective descriptions and category attributes, or update existing codes. When adding or updating a code, you'll enter a code number and description, and specify whether the code is related to immunization. Any validation errors during this process will be displayed, enabling you to correct the inputs. The system also presents a list of current CPT codes, allowing you to view detailed descriptions and attributes, and easily select existing entries for updating. This functionality is essential for ensuring accuracy and compliance within healthcare billing practices, aiding efficient administrative management of procedure documentation.

WebRoot/auth/admin/editICDCodes.jsp: As an administrator using this system to maintain medical diagnosis codes, you would be overseeing the updating and adding of ICD (International Classification of Diseases) codes. Your primary task involves managing the code database which includes specifying a code, indicating if the condition is chronic, and providing a description. When you want to add a new code or update an existing one, you input the necessary details and submit. Upon successful addition or update, a confirmation message will be displayed. In case of a validation error, a message will notify you, prompting you to correct the input. Current ICD codes are displayed in a list for review, and you can select a code to update by clicking on it, which fills the form with that code's present details for modification. This system ensures that the ICD code database is kept current and accurate for diagnostic referencing.

WebRoot/auth/admin/editLOINCCodes.jsp:
As an administrator using this system, you would:

Manage and update the list of diagnostic laboratory codes known as LOINC codes, which are critical for consistent lab results retrieval.

You can view the current list of LOINC codes, including their respective components, properties, time aspects, systems, scale types, and methods.

To add a new LOINC code, fill in the necessary fields, such as lab procedure code, component, kind of property, time aspect, system, scale type, and method type. Then submit the form for the code to be added to the list.

To update an existing LOINC code's details, click on the code from the list and the form fields will auto-fill with its current information. Make any necessary changes and then submit the form to update the code's details.

Review confirmation messages indicating success or error in code additions or updates, so you can ensure accuracy and completeness in the LOINC codes system.

This interface enables administrators to efficiently manage LOINC code entries, which are fundamental in ensuring data standardization across lab results and procedures.

WebRoot/auth/admin/editNDCInteractions.j: As an administrator using this system, you can manage interactions between drugs based on their ND Codes. Firstly, you select two drugs from the respective dropdowns, where each is represented by its ND Code along with its description. After selecting the drugs, you provide a description detailing the nature of the interaction you want to report. Once you submit, the system processes and records this potential interaction in the database, allowing you to maintain an updated record of drug interactions. If there are form errors or validation issues, appropriate error messages will be displayed to help you correct them. You can always navigate back to the main list of ND Codes if needed. This functionality helps in ensuring patient safety by tracking and alerting drug combinations that may lead to adverse reactions.

WebRoot/auth/admin/editNDCodes.jsp:
As a healthcare administrator using this system, you can efficiently manage the National Drug Code (NDC) list and update drug interactions. To maintain the ND Codes:

1. View the current ND Codes along with their descriptions in a comprehensive list.
2. Add a new ND Code by entering the code parts and description, ensuring accurate categorization of medication within the system.
3. Update existing ND Codes if any drug's information needs correction or enhancement by choosing the specific code and modifying its description.
4. Delete an interaction between drugs if necessary, ensuring that the system maintains only relevant and current interactions.
5. Check interactions for each ND Code, which helps to understand potential interactions that could affect patient health.
6. Utilize an intuitive interface to fill in or modify details; interactions for each drug will appear to aid you in making informed updates.
7. For further refinement in relationships between drugs, follow the provided link to directly edit interactions.

This process ensures precise and current pharmaceutical data management, promoting safe medication practices within the organization.

WebRoot/auth/admin/home.jsp: As an admin using this system, you would visit the home page where you'll receive a personalized welcome message with your name. This page serves as your gateway to the system, likely allowing you to navigate to various administrative functions and manage tasks within the application. This simple and welcoming setup ensures you have immediate recognition and a user-friendly interface to begin your administrative duties.

WebRoot/auth/admin/hospitalAssignments.j: As an administrator managing hospital staff assignments within this healthcare system, you would utilize the interface to manage the assignments of healthcare personnel (HCP) to hospitals. First, ensure that a valid personnel ID (PID) is entered; otherwise, the system redirects to another page to obtain this ID. Once the PID is verified, you can view two sections: "Assigned Hospitals" and "Available Hospitals." In the "Assigned Hospitals" section, you can see the list of hospitals currently assigned to the HCP. Here, you have the option to "Unassign" the HCP from a hospital, effectively updating their assignment status. In the "Available Hospitals" section, you can view hospitals to which the HCP can be assigned. Clicking "Assign" next to a hospital adds it to the HCP's list of assigned hospitals. This system facilitates efficient management and updating of hospital staffing assignments, ensuring the right personnel are always aligned with the appropriate hospitals.

WebRoot/auth/admin/hospitalListing.jsp:
As a healthcare administrator using this system, you would:
Maintain an up-to-date listing of hospitals by adding new hospitals or updating the information of existing ones.
You can enter the hospital's ID and name in the form provided. The hospital list you maintain is then displayed for your review.
To add a new hospital, input the hospital's details and click "Add Hospital." To update information, select a hospital from the list, fill in the desired changes, and click "Update Hospital Information."
If you make any errors during the update, such as invalid information, a validation error message will appear to inform you, allowing corrections.
The current list of hospitals will be displayed with the ability to quickly select and edit hospital information directly within the interface.
This tool helps streamline the management of hospital records, ensuring accuracy and accessibility for hospital administrators.

WebRoot/auth/admin/information.jsp:
As an administrative user using this system, you would:
Log into the system to view your personal information profile.
See your profile picture displayed, which can help to personalize the interface.
View your name as stored in the system to ensure your profile details are updated accurately.
This setup provides a simple overview for administrative users to manage and review their profile details within the organization swiftly.

WebRoot/auth/admin/menu.jsp: As an administrator using this system, you have access to multiple functionalities to manage healthcare operations efficiently. You can add new personnel such as healthcare providers, emergency responders, and public health authorities to the system. You can edit various system settings such as appointment types, hospital assignments, and procedural codes. The system allows you to send out appointment reminders to patients, ensuring they are kept up to date with scheduled visits. You also have tools to edit personnel information and manage hospital listings effectively. Furthermore, you have access to system reminders and can review satisfaction survey results, which help in assessing patient feedback. Lastly, you can manage session settings like the global session timeout to ensure security and optimize system operations. This menu offers a comprehensive set of options to support healthcare administration tasks and deliver quality service.

WebRoot/auth/admin/remindersMessageOutbo:
As an administrator using this system, you would:  
Access a dedicated section to view the outbox containing reminder messages you have sent.  
The system provides options to sort the messages by recipient name or send time, and in either ascending or descending order, allowing you to organize the data according to your preference.  
If there are any messages, each line will display the recipient's name, the subject of the message, the date it was sent, and an option to read the full message. Unread messages will be in bold to help you easily identify them.  
If there are no messages, the system will inform you that your message outbox is empty.  
This functionality facilitates efficient management of reminder messages you've sent, enabling you to keep track of your communications effectively.

WebRoot/auth/admin/sendAppointmentRemind: As an administrator using this system, you would navigate to the appointment reminder functionality to ensure upcoming appointments are communicated to patients efficiently. Begin by entering the number of days prior to appointments within which reminders should be sent. Upon submission, the system will review all scheduled appointments during the specified period. For each appointment, the system will send a reminder message to the corresponding patient, detailing the appointment date and the assigned healthcare provider. The outcome, such as the number of messages successfully sent or error notifications for incorrect input, will be displayed, allowing you to confirm that reminders were correctly dispatched. This feature aids in maintaining appointment attendance and reducing missed appointments, thereby enhancing operational efficiency and patient care.

WebRoot/auth/admin/sessionTimeout.jsp: As an administrator using this system, you would access this feature to manage the session timeout settings for user accounts. You can set the duration by specifying the number of minutes an account can remain inactive before requiring re-authentication. Simply enter the desired timeout duration in the provided input field and submit the changes. If the input is valid, the system will update the session timeout, and the new setting will take effect when users re-authenticate. This functionality helps in ensuring adequate security measures through session management.

WebRoot/auth/admin/viewAllReportRequests:
As an administrator using this system, you would:
Access a list of all pending and completed report requests from patients for review and approval.
For each request, see details such as the patient’s name, the approver’s name, the dates the report was requested, approved, and viewed, along with its current status and any comments attached.
You are provided with options to approve or reject the requests that are still pending approval.
Upon approving a request, the system will mark it as approved, showing a confirmation message.
If rejecting, you will need to provide a reason in the comment section. After confirmation, the request will be marked as rejected with the reason logged.
This system allows you to efficiently manage and track report requests, ensuring proper authorization before any sensitive information is shared.

WebRoot/auth/admin/viewReminderMessage.j: As a system administrator using this feature, you would: Access a specific reminder message that has been sent from your outbox. The system retrieves the message details using an index parameter which helps in identifying the precise message. You'll view information such as the recipient's name, as determined by the extracted sender's ID from the message subject line, the subject line itself, and the date and time the message was sent. The body of the message will also be displayed for review. If the message is not specified correctly by the system, it defaults to sending you back to the overview of sent reminder messages. This function lets you efficiently organize and track communications within the system.

WebRoot/auth/admin/visitGraph.jsp: As an administrator using this system, you would: Select the start and end months and years to generate a report on the visits to the healthcare facility. Submit the selected date range, and the system will validate the entered dates to ensure the start date is before the end date and both dates are valid (not in the future). If valid, the system generates a graph showing trends in visit data over the selected period. This graph visually represents the number of visits per month for two categories: minors and adults. Hover over or reference the graph to analyze the data patterns and identify periods with the highest and lowest visits, allowing for better resource allocation and planning. If there was an error in date selection (like the end date being in the future), the system will alert you with an error message, guiding you to correct the input and try again. The graphical report is a tool for understanding visit trends over time, aiding in operational and strategic decisions for the facility.

WebRoot/auth/er/home.jsp: As an Emergency Room (ER) personnel using this system, you will arrive at a home page specifically designed for your role. Here, you will find important announcements about new features and improvements in the system, enhancing your ability to perform tasks efficiently. The page highlights user interface enhancements, such as the addition of a calendar pop-up that simplifies the process of setting dates, reducing time spent on data entry. Additionally, a notifications section is provided, which may display relevant alerts or updates pertaining to your functions or the healthcare facility. This homepage serves as a central point for keeping ER personnel informed and equipped with tools for improved productivity and patient care management. You can easily navigate to other parts of the system to continue with your emergency room responsibilities.

WebRoot/auth/er/information.jsp: As a registered employee using this system, you would access your personal profile information. Once logged in, you will see your profile picture and basic details such as your full name and location, including the city and state you are based in. This feature helps you verify and review your personal information easily.

WebRoot/auth/er/menu.jsp: As an Emergency Room (ER) personnel using this system, you would navigate through the menu to access the Emergency Patient Report to efficiently manage patient information related to emergency cases. This option allows you to quickly retrieve critical patient data and reports, aiding in providing timely and effective emergency care services.

WebRoot/auth/exceptionHandler.jsp:
As a user experiencing an error on the healthcare management system, you would:
Encounter an unexpected issue that interrupts the normal operation, such as a failed data operation or access problem.
The system will automatically capture the error details and record them for diagnostic purposes.
You will be redirected to a specific page designed to guide you to the appropriate section post-error, ensuring minimal disruption to your workflow.
This system enhances reliability by offering a user-friendly approach to manage and recover from errors.

WebRoot/auth/forwardUser.jsp: As a user of this system, once you log in, you will be directed to the home page that corresponds to your role. For example, if you're a patient, you'll be directed to the patient's home page where you can access health information relevant to you. If you're a healthcare provider, you'll be taken to a home page containing clinical tools and patient records needed for your daily tasks. Similarly, other roles such as User Access Personnel, Emergency Responder, Public Health Authority, Administrator, or Tester have their distinct home pages ensuring they have access to functionalities unique to their responsibilities. If your role is not recognized, you may experience restricted access, leading to a page that highlights access issues. Additionally, invalid sessions or non-existent user IDs may result in the termination of your session or a redirection back to the login page to ensure the security of user information. This system ensures each user has swift access to the tools and data needed for their specific functions.

WebRoot/auth/getPatientID.jsp:
As a user of this system, you would interact in the following manner to select or search for a patient:
You start by selecting or searching for a patient in the system. To search, you input the patient's first name and/or last name into the search fields provided.
Once the names are entered, you initiate the search by clicking the "User Search" button. The system will display a list of patients that match the search criteria along with their medical IDs.
To select a specific patient from the list, you simply click on the corresponding medical ID. This action will direct you to another page determined by the value in the "forward" parameter, allowing you to proceed with viewing or managing the selected patient's information.
This patient selection process helps you to efficiently search and choose a patient for further interactions or detailed data access, ensuring smooth navigation within the healthcare management system.

WebRoot/auth/getPersonnelID.jsp: As a user of this healthcare system tasked with the role of identifying personnel, you would utilize this process to select a healthcare professional from the system efficiently. You begin by accessing a screen where you are prompted to specify search criteria, such as first and last name, to locate the Personnel. If you already know the Personnel ID, you can directly enter this information to proceed. Once you input a search query, the system will search and display a list of personnel who match the specified names. The results are shown in a table with records providing personnel details such as their unique ID, first name, and last name. Each record includes a button that allows you to select a specific personnel, facilitating easy identification and selection. The system then utilizes the selected personnel's ID to redirect you to another business-related function or page, thereby streamlining the workflow for personnel management and identification within the healthcare system. This process ensures that only authorized personnel information is accessed and used, maintaining data security and integrity.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/addUAP.jsp: As a healthcare provider using this system to add a new User Access Personnel (UAP), you would: Fill in the form with the UAP's first name, last name, and a valid email address. If the UAP doesn't have an email, substitute it with the hospital's predefined email to ensure password recovery is possible. Upon submission of the form, the system will create a new UAP profile, assigning them a unique Medical ID (MID) and a temporary password. You will receive a confirmation message containing the new UAP's MID and temporary password for you to communicate to them personally. This streamlined process allows you to efficiently onboard new personnel while ensuring secure handling of access credentials.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/calendar.jsp:
As a healthcare provider using this system, you would:

View your appointment calendar, which allows you to manage and keep track of scheduled appointments for the current month.
Navigate between months using the "Last" and "Next" links to view past and upcoming months' appointments.
Each day in the calendar will display appointments scheduled for that date, with a convenient link to "Read Details" for each appointment, allowing you to view more information.
If an appointment has conflicting schedules or issues, it will be visibly highlighted for immediate attention.
This calendar helps you efficiently plan your daily, weekly, and monthly schedules by clearly presenting your engagements and potential conflicts upfront.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/editPatientList.jsp: As a healthcare provider using this system, you manage the list of patients who require monitoring. Initially, you select a patient whose monitoring status you wish to adjust. If the patient exists in the current monitoring list, you have the option to remove them; if they are not on the list, you can add them. When you confirm the action, the system updates the patient’s monitoring status and notifies you with a confirmation message indicating whether the patient was added or removed from the list. You also have the flexibility to choose a different patient if needed before finalizing your decision. This functionality helps maintain an accurate list of monitored patients, ensuring effective management of their healthcare needs.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/editRepresentatives.jsp: As a healthcare provider, you are able to manage patient representation within your system. First, you must ensure that you have selected a valid patient. Once a patient is selected, you can view their current list of representatives. If there are no representatives, this will be clearly indicated. For each representative, you have the option to remove them if they are no longer needed. Additionally, you can add a new representative for the patient by searching for a user, selecting them, and confirming your choice. This system is designed to let you efficiently manage the representatives to ensure that the patient's information is accessed and handled by the appropriate individuals.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/hcpConsultation.jsp:
As a healthcare provider (HCP) using this system, you would be able to manage consultations with other providers efficiently. Initially, you have options to either send a new consultation request or view pending consultations. In sending a consultation, you can refer a patient to another HCP by selecting from the list of your patients and choosing another provider for the referral. Once selected, you will fill out details regarding the referral and send it.

You can also review consultations that are either outgoing or incoming. Outgoing consultations are those you have referred, while incoming consultations are those referred to you. Each consultation has its current status (pending, finished, or declined) and can be edited depending on its status and the consultation's details.

In updating consultations, you can modify the status and relevant details of a referral. If details from the other HCP or patient are missing, the system ensures you are informed, allowing smooth communication. This organized approach to managing consultations helps in maintaining seamless patient care and collaboration between healthcare providers.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/home.jsp:
As a healthcare provider (HCP) using this system, you would use your home portal to stay updated on various aspects of your practice. The portal offers a section for announcements regarding new system features, such as a user-friendly calendar popup for date selection. Notifications are also presented, where you can review comprehensive report histories, highlighting recent report requests you've made. If there are any report requests pending action, they will be listed for you to follow up on.

Additionally, the portal provides details about lab procedures that have been completed within the last month, along with a link to view all procedures. For each lab procedure, the patient's name and procedure ID are displayed. You’ll be able to see the procedure results, or be alerted if no results have been entered. This setup allows you to efficiently monitor patient lab procedures and manage report requests, making it easier to keep track of critical tasks and patient information within your healthcare practice.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/information.jsp: As a healthcare provider using this system, you can view your personal profile information. Upon accessing the page, you will see your profile picture along with your full name and the location of your practice, including the city and state. This personalized information helps you confirm your identity and details in the system, ensuring that you have quick access to your professional data while using the healthcare platform.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/LabProcHCP.jsp: As a healthcare provider utilizing this system, you will be able to view and manage laboratory procedures for patients under your care. First, you must access a patient's record by their unique ID. If the ID is missing or incorrect, the system will redirect you to obtain the correct patient identifier. Once authenticated with the patient ID, you can see a list of lab procedures associated with the patient. For each procedure, you can review various details including the lab code, rights granted on the procedure, current status, any commentary or results available, the associated office visit ID, and the date it was last updated. The system allows you to edit the office visit details if you have the appropriate access rights. You also have the ability to change the privacy settings of the lab procedure, allowing you to control who can view it. Additionally, there is an option to update the procedure's information if needed. If no data is available for the procedures, the system will clearly communicate this to you. This setup ensures that you manage your patient's laboratory information effectively while maintaining control over access to sensitive data.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/menu.jsp:
As a healthcare provider (HCP) using this system, you are provided with a comprehensive set of functionalities accessible through a menu. These activities are categorized for clarity and ease of use:

1. Under the "Add" section, you can initiate the process to add new patients or User Access Personnel (UAP).

2. The "Edit" section allows you to update information, such as basic health details, your demographic data, patient information, and personal health records (PHR). You can also manage representatives and UAP records.

3. With "Appointments," you have the capacity to schedule new appointments and view your schedule.

4. The "Messaging" area provides access to your message inbox and outbox, facilitating communication with other professionals or patients.

5. The "View" category includes options to review all patients' office visit histories, see your appointment calendar, check laboratory procedures, and handle report requests.

6. Under "Report," you can generate emergency patient reports.

7. The "Telemedicine" section offers capabilities to manage a patient list specific to telemedicine and remotely monitor patient data.

8. Finally, "Other" functionalities include managing consultations, assessing chronic disease risks, documenting office visits, tracking email history, sending office visit reminders, reviewing satisfaction survey results, and overseeing prescription renewal needs.

These diverse categories ensure that you can efficiently manage both administrative and clinical tasks, facilitating streamlined patient care and data management.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/messageInbox.jsp:
As a healthcare provider using this system, you can manage and interact with your message inbox effectively. Here's how you can use this feature:

View your list of messages, which will be displayed in a table format showing the sender, subject, and received date of each message. Unread messages will appear in bold to distinguish them from those you have already read.

You have the option to sort these messages by sender name or received time in ascending or descending order, making it easier to find specific messages or see the latest communications first.

If you want to focus on certain messages or hide others, you can use the filtering options. Filters can be created based on criteria such as sender, subject, specific words the message should or should not contain, and date periods. You can edit and test these filters before saving them, which helps you control which messages are shown in your inbox.

For each message, you can click a "Read" link that will take you to a detailed view of the message, where you can read the full content of the communication.

These tools help you efficiently manage communication within the healthcare system, ensuring you can stay on top of important information while minimizing clutter.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/messageOutbox.jsp: As a healthcare provider (HCP) using this system, you would: Access your outbox to view all the messages you have sent. You can sort these sent messages based on the recipient's name or the time they were sent, and choose the order as ascending or descending. Click the button to apply your sorting preference. View a list of sent messages displaying the recipient, subject, and sent date of each message. For detailed information, click on the "Read" link next to a message to open and read the full content. If you have no sent messages, a notification will inform you that your outbox is empty. There is also a convenient link for composing a new message, facilitating clear communication with patients or colleagues. This system optimizes your communications by allowing you to effortlessly track and manage sent messages for better organizational workflow.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/monitorPatients.jsp: As a healthcare provider using this system, you would access a list of patients under your care with remotely monitored health data. The list provides detailed information for each patient, such as their blood pressure and glucose levels, along with the date when the data was recorded. The system automatically highlights patients whose current day's data is missing in red, and those with abnormal health readings in yellow, allowing you to prioritize those patients. For more detailed information on a patient's condition, you can select their name from the list. This feature enables the efficient monitoring of patients’ health metrics and assists in quickly identifying potential health issues that require your attention.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/reply.jsp: As a healthcare provider, you can quickly respond to a message from a patient using this system. After entering the reply page, you will see the subject pre-filled with "RE:" followed by the original subject, allowing you to maintain clarity in the conversation thread. You can then type your message in the provided text area. Once you're ready to send your response, simply click the “Send” button. The system will direct the message to the patient's inbox while ensuring the conversation continuity by linking your reply to the original message. This streamlined process helps you communicate efficiently with your patients, ensuring timely and organized correspondence.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/scheduleAppt.jsp:
As a healthcare provider using this system, you would:
Select a patient for whom you want to schedule an appointment. If no patient is selected, you will be redirected to choose a patient from the list.
Fill out the appointment form by selecting the type and duration of the appointment from a list of available types.
Choose a date and time for the appointment that suits both you and the patient. You have the option to specify the time in hours, minutes, and whether it is AM or PM.
Optionally, add some comments to provide additional context or information related to the appointment.
Once the form is complete, click the schedule button to book the appointment.
The system will then process the booking and send a confirmation message. If successful, you will be redirected to your homepage, where you can manage other appointments. If any errors occur, such as invalid data formats, the system will display error messages prompting you to correct them.
This process ensures that appointments are accurately scheduled according to patient and healthcare provider availability, enhancing the efficiency of office management.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/sendEmailNotification.j: As a healthcare provider using this system, you can send email notifications to patients. First, you will select a patient from your roster whose Medical ID (MID) is available. After selection, the patient's email address and name will be automatically filled into the email form. You can customize the subject and message before sending the email. You need to provide personalized information in the email text to remind or inform the patient. Once you submit the form, the email is sent using the details provided, and you will receive a confirmation indicating that the email was sent successfully. After sending the email, you will have the option to return to your home page to continue with other tasks. This system makes it easier for healthcare providers to communicate important information directly to patients, ensuring streamlined and efficient healthcare service notifications.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/sendMessage.jsp: As a healthcare provider using this system, you can easily communicate with your patients through secure messaging. If you want to send a message, you first choose the patient you wish to contact. If you haven't selected a patient, the system will prompt you to do so. Once a patient is selected, you can compose your message by entering a subject and the message content. After writing your message, you can send it directly to the patient. Should you enter any invalid information, the system will alert you so you can correct it before sending. This tool streamlines communication, allowing you to stay in touch with patients effectively while keeping records of messages sent.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/UpdateLabProc.jsp: As a healthcare provider using this system, you would update lab procedure details for your patients. You would start by selecting the specific lab procedure you wish to update. Once selected, you can modify the procedure's status, provide additional commentary, and enter the results of the lab. After making the necessary updates, you submit the form to save the changes. The system will confirm that the information was updated successfully. This allows you to efficiently manage and document lab procedures while keeping all necessary details up-to-date for future reference.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/viewAdditionalInfo.jsp: As a healthcare provider utilizing this system, you would: Select a patient from your list to view detailed assessments of their remote monitoring data, which include blood pressure readings and glucose levels. Within the patient's details, you also gain access to their representatives, and these are presented should the patient require assistance in managing their health information. For periods when the physiological data was recorded, you can specify a date range to retrieve the patient's health statistics such as systolic and diastolic blood pressure, glucose levels, and the name of the reporter who recorded the data. The system provides visual alerts: days with missing data are highlighted in red, while days with abnormal readings are in yellow, helping to prioritize your review of patient records. This functionality aids in maintaining high-quality monitoring of patient health data, enhancing patient care through informed decisions.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/viewAppt.jsp:
As a healthcare provider using this system, you would:
Utilize the system to view detailed information about your appointment with a patient, which includes the patient's name, the type of appointment scheduled, the date and time of the appointment, and its duration. You will also see any comments related to the appointment. If the appointment details are not accessible initially, the system redirects you to another page listing your appointments or notifies you of an error. This setup ensures that you can verify appointment details and plan accordingly for your patient's visit.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/viewMessageInbox.jsp:
As a healthcare provider (HCP) using this system, you would:
Navigate to your message inbox to view individual messages sent by patients or other staff members.
If you select a message from the inbox, the system will display the details of the message including the sender's name, the subject, and the date and time it was sent. Additionally, the content of the message is shown.
Once you view a message, the system marks it as read.
You have the option to reply to the message, making communication direct and efficient.
This system facilitates secure and efficient communication between healthcare providers and patients, ensuring timely response and action on important health-related communications.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/viewMessageOutbox.jsp:
As a healthcare provider (HCP) using this system, you would:
Navigate to your outbox to view messages you have sent.
Select a specific message to see the details, including the recipient's name, the subject, and the date and time it was sent.
Read the message content within the familiar user interface.
If no message is selected, the system will guide you back to your message list.
This functionality helps ensure clear communication and record-keeping of your interactions with patients or colleagues.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/viewMyAppts.jsp:
As a healthcare provider using this system, you would:
Access your scheduled appointments to view details about each appointment including patient names, appointment types, date and time, and duration.
The system checks for any overlapping appointments, which are displayed with bold highlighting to alert you to potential scheduling conflicts.
For appointments with comments or special notes, the system provides a link to view these comments in detail.
If no appointments are scheduled, the system informs you accordingly.
This process enables you to manage and review your appointments efficiently, ensuring that any conflicts are promptly identified and addressed to maintain smooth scheduling and patient care.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/viewMyMessages.jsp:
As a healthcare provider using this system, you would:

Log in to your account and navigate to the section where you can view messages sent to you. These messages could be from patients or other healthcare professionals.
Upon accessing the page, you'll see a list of all your received messages if there are any. This page provides an overview, showing the sender, content of the message, and the date when it was received.
If you have messages, you can choose to reply to each message by clicking the 'Reply' link provided. This will take you to a page where you can compose and send your reply.
If you have no messages, the system will clearly indicate that your inbox is empty.
The system supports efficient communication by allowing you to view and respond to messages quickly, maintaining clear communication with patients and colleagues in a healthcare setting.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/viewPrescriptionRenewal:
As a healthcare provider using this system, you would:
Access a list of patients whose prescriptions may need renewal based on your logged-in status as the responsible provider.
For each patient, view their name, phone number, and email address, which are displayed in a table format for easy reference.
If there are no patients who require prescription renewals, a message will indicate that no action is required.
You can select a patient's name to send an email notification regarding their prescription renewal needs.
This process helps you proactively manage patient prescriptions, ensuring medications are renewed in a timely manner and reducing the risk of interruptions in treatment.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/visitReminders.jsp:
As a healthcare provider using this system, you would:
Select the type of reminder you want to view from a dropdown menu. This may include various categories such as upcoming visits, checkup reminders, or other healthcare prompts.
Upon selecting and submitting your choice, the system will display a list of patients who need visits based on the selected reminder type.
For each patient, you’ll see their name, phone number, and reasons detailing why a visit is necessary.
The patient’s name is linked to an option to send an email notification directly to remind them of their visit needs.
This functionality enables you to efficiently manage patient visit reminders, thereby ensuring patients receive timely care and you maintain effective communication.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-er/emergencyReport.jsp:
As a healthcare provider (ER staff) using this system during an emergency, you would:  
Access a patient's emergency report by initially entering the patient's ID. If the ID is valid, the system retrieves emergency-specific medical information for you to review.  
You have the ability to print the emergency report, ensuring you have a hard copy of the patient’s critical health information.  
The system automatically notifies all declared healthcare providers (HCPs) of the patient, via email, that the patient’s record has been accessed in an emergency context. This maintains a collaborative communication loop among all relevant medical personnel.  
Within the report, you will see the patient’s demographic details, such as name, age, and gender, as well as their emergency contact information.  
The report provides detailed lists of any known allergies, medical diagnoses, current prescriptions, and immunization history, crucial for quick reference and decision-making in an emergency situation.  
Any warnings or alerts related to diagnoses or medications are prioritized to help you quickly assess any critical health issues that need immediate attention.  
This functionality ensures that, as an ER staff member, you are equipped with comprehensive and up-to-date patient information critical to delivering appropriate and immediate care during emergencies.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/addPatient.jsp: As a healthcare provider (HCP) using this system, you would: Enter the patient's first name, last name, and email address into the form. After submitting the form, the system will create a new patient record and assign a unique Medical ID (MID) to the patient. The system will also generate a temporary password, which you can provide to the patient for them to reset their password later. You’ll see a confirmation message with the patient's MID and temporary password, and you’ll be prompted to continue managing the patient's information through another page. You cannot edit or view the patient's security details such as their password or security question. This process ensures that the new patient is added securely, with minimal input required from you, while protecting sensitive information like security questions and passwords.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/chronicDiseaseRisks: As a healthcare provider or user access personnel using this system, you would start by selecting a patient whose chronic disease risk factors you want to review. If you haven't selected a patient yet, the system will redirect you to a page to enter the patient's ID. Once the patient's ID is set, the system will retrieve the patient's chronic disease risk factors. You can view a list of diseases the patient might be at risk for, along with detailed risk factors associated with each disease. This allows you to identify potential health risks and prioritize care for patients based on their specific risk factors. The system ensures accurate assessment of risks, facilitating proactive management of chronic diseases based on tailored health insights.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/documentOfficeVisit: As a healthcare provider using this system, you can: Identify the patient for whom you want to document an office visit. Confirm that you wish to create a new office visit record for the patient by clicking the 'Yes, Document Office Visit' button. This action will generate a new entry for the office visit, which you can later modify with specific details of the visit. In addition to creating new records, you have access to the patient's past office visit records. By clicking on a previous visit date, you can review and update the details for any past visits. This system facilitates efficient management of office visit documentation and ensures that all patient interactions are accurately recorded and easily accessible for future reference.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/editBasicHealth.jsp: As a healthcare provider or user access personnel, you would access this system to manage and update a patient's basic health records. You first need to ensure you have the patient's ID, and if it's not available, the system redirects you to a page where you can retrieve this ID. Once you have access, you can view the patient's detailed health history including their height, weight, smoking status, blood pressure, cholesterol levels, and the date of the last recorded data along with the name of the personnel who recorded it. You can add new health records by clicking a button to reveal a form where you input new details. The system allows you to update these records conveniently, using the most recent values as default inputs for any new record entry, helping maintain accurate health data for each patient over time. Error messages guide you to correct any mistakes during the record input process, ensuring data accuracy and integrity.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/editOfficeVisit.jsp:
As a healthcare provider using this system, you would:

Begin by selecting a patient's existing office visit record that you want to edit. If the patient ID is not specified, you will be redirected to select or input a patient ID first.

You'll be able to view and update various details regarding the office visit, including the date of visit, hospital, and notes associated with the visit.

If you need to prescribe medication for the patient, the system allows you to select medication from a comprehensive list, specifying details like dosage, start and end dates of the prescription, along with any special instructions.

To avoid any adverse drug interactions or allergy reactions, the system checks the prescribed medication against the patient's records, highlighting any potential warnings so you can confirm or cancel the prescription.

Additionally, you can manage laboratory procedures linked to the office visit, add new lab procedures, update statuses, and remove outdated procedures.

You can also add, update, or remove diagnoses, procedures, and immunizations associated with the visit. The system provides lists from which you can select diagnoses based on ICD codes, procedures based on CPT codes, and immunizations.

Upon submission, the updated information is saved and can be instantly viewed or further managed. Notifications can be set up to inform patients of updates to their prescriptions, ensuring they are always aware of any new medications or changes.

This functionality helps ensure comprehensive and safe management of a patient's healthcare records during office visits, optimizing the process for healthcare providers by integrating checks for allergies and medication interactions while updating patient care details seamlessly.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/editPatient.jsp:
As a healthcare provider using this system, you would:
Access the patient's records by first selecting the patient ID, ensuring that the correct individual is being updated.
Once verified, you will proceed to edit various personal, contact, health, and insurance details of the patient.
You can update basic information like name, email, address, and phone numbers, as well as more sensitive details like medical data, including blood type, ethnicity, and gender.
Other fields that can be edited include the patient's emergency contact information, insurance details, and health records such as topical notes or historical diagnosis codes.
For deceased patients, you may enter the date of death and cause of death.
This allows you to comprehensively manage a patient's medical and personal records, ensuring all changes are accurately logged.
Once the information is updated, you will receive a confirmation message.
Password changes are handled separately through a password reset function accessible on the system’s login page.
This process provides streamlined, secure management of patient demographics and health-related records, which is crucial for maintaining updated patient information.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/editPatientList.jsp:
As a healthcare provider using this system, you would:  
First ensure that you have a patient's Medical ID (MID) available as it is required to proceed.  
If the patient ID is not found or provided, the system will redirect you to obtain the patient ID before continuing.  
Once a valid patient ID is recognized, the system will display whether the patient is currently on your monitoring list.  
Based on their current status, you'll see an option to either "Add" or "Remove" the patient from your list.  
Confirming this action will either add the patient to or remove them from your monitoring list, and the system will confirm your action with a message stating the change.  
Additionally, you have the option to opt for a different patient if needed, prompting the system to reset the patient ID and let you select another patient for editing.  
This tool facilitates easy management and monitoring of your patient's list, ensuring that their status is up to date with your professional monitoring activities.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/editPHR.jsp: As a healthcare professional using this system, you can efficiently manage and update a patient's personal health records through a comprehensive interface. Start by accessing the patient's record, where you can view and edit detailed personal information such as contact details and insurance provider information. You can also review the patient's basic health records, including height, weight, smoking status, blood pressure, and cholesterol levels. If there is any new health information, such as allergies or chronic disease risk factors, you can add or update it using the provided forms. The system allows you to examine the patient's family medical history to assess genetic risk factors. Furthermore, you can navigate through the patient's office visit history and even view the details of any chronic disease threats. The system organizes this information to streamline patient care, making it easy for you to maintain accurate and up-to-date medical records.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/editPrescription.js: As a healthcare provider using this system, you would begin by selecting a specific patient and their associated office visit to access the current prescriptions. Should you need to update a prescription, you can initiate an edit process directly from the displayed list of medications. Upon selecting a prescription, you will be provided with a form where you can adjust details such as the dosage and any special instructions for use. Once you have made the desired changes, you can submit the form to update the prescription while ensuring the medication's start and end dates remain the same. If the update is successful, you will see a confirmation message with the revised prescription details. If the system encounters any issue during the process, an error message will display, allowing you to attempt the update again. This functionality ensures that prescription information remains current and accurate, supporting patient care by providing clear and accessible medication instructions.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/getPrescriptionRepo: As a healthcare provider (HCP) or User Access Personnel (UAP) using this system, you would: Start by ensuring that a patient's unique identification is available in the session. If not, you will be redirected to a page to input or select a patient ID before you can proceed. Once the patient's ID is validated, you will be presented with a comprehensive report of all their prescriptions. This report includes details such as the National Drug Code (ND Code) for each prescribed medication, a description of the medication, the duration for which the prescription is valid, and the healthcare provider who prescribed it. In cases where there are no prescriptions found for the patient, a message indicating the absence of prescriptions is displayed. This detailed prescription report facilitates the management and review of a patient's medication history, ensuring that you have all necessary information to support effective health care delivery.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/LabProcUAP.jsp:
As a healthcare provider (HCP) accessing this system, you would:  
First, identify the patient whose laboratory procedures you want to view. If a patient's ID is not selected, the system will prompt you to choose one.  
Once the patient is selected, you can view a detailed table displaying the patient's lab procedures. This table includes essential information such as lab codes, current rights, status, any added commentary, results, and the associated Office Visit ID, which helps in correlating procedures with specific patient visits.   
The table also shows the last date when the procedure data was updated, providing insights into the timeliness of the data.  
If you need to make updates to any lab procedure details, the system provides an option to update the information directly from the table, streamlining the workflow.  
This system aids in effectively managing and reviewing laboratory data for patients, ensuring that all relevant information is easily accessible for analysis and updates.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/showEmailHistory.js: As a medical personnel using this system, you can view the historical records of emails that have been sent and received. The system presents these records in the form of a table, displaying details for each email including the recipients, subject, content of the email, and the date it was sent. If no emails are found in the records, the system will inform you that there are no emails on record. This helps you quickly access and track communication history within the medical context for transparency and documentation purposes.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/updateLabProc.jsp: As a healthcare provider updating lab procedures using this system, you would start by accessing the specific lab procedure record through a unique identifier provided to you. Once you access this record, you have the opportunity to update three critical fields: the status of the lab procedure, any commentary you wish to add, and the results of the lab procedure. When you complete the updates and submit the form, the system processes your input and updates the lab procedure information. Upon successful updating, the system confirms that the information has been updated successfully, ensuring that the latest details are accurately reflected in the system for further medical processes or patient review. If any issues arise, such as an incorrect form submission, an error message will guide you in rectifying the issue. This mechanism allows for efficient management of patient lab procedure data, ensuring that it is current and readily available for necessary healthcare decisions.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/viewMyReportRequest: As a healthcare provider (HCP) or user access personnel (UAP) using this system, you can view, manage, and fulfill report requests for patients under your care. You'll see a list of all past report requests you've made, along with details such as the patient’s name, the date the report was requested, the date it was viewed, and the current status of each request. For any pending request, you can click on the "View" link to see detailed information contained in the report. Additionally, you have the option to initiate a new report request for a patient by clicking on the provided link, which will take you to a page where you can select a patient and submit your request. This functionality supports efficient tracking and management of patient reports, ensuring you have timely access to the information needed for patient care decisions.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/viewPatientOfficeVi: As a healthcare provider, you can view a list of patients who have visited your practice. The system provides a straightforward view with each patient's name, address, and the date of their last visit. You can click on a patient’s name to access their personal health record for updates or further actions. This function helps you maintain comprehensive records of patient interactions and aids in reviewing histories for ongoing or follow-up care. It is tailored to support efficient patient management in outpatient clinics or private practices.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/viewReport.jsp: As a healthcare professional using this system, you will be able to generate comprehensive reports for patients. You can select a patient based on their unique identifier to view and verify the request for generating a report. The report will provide detailed information including personal and insurance details of the patient like name, address, phone, and email. Additionally, the system will display health records showing metrics like height, weight, blood pressure, cholesterol levels, and smoking status, along with the personnel who recorded this data. You can also see a list of diagnoses, procedures, prescriptions, office visits, family relationships, allergies, healthcare providers related to the patient, and any representation details regarding the patient. These details are structured section by section, helping you evaluate the comprehensive health status of the patient efficiently. Should any information be missing or incorrect, you will be able to recognize these gaps for further investigation or correction. This system facilitates in-depth patient assessments through structured reporting that supports patient management and care planning.

WebRoot/auth/patient/addTelemedicineData:
As a patient or their designated representative using this system, you would:

Be able to report telemedicine data such as blood pressure (systolic and diastolic) and glucose levels. If you are a patient, you can report your own data, or you may report data for someone you represent, such as a family member.

Simply input the relevant physiological data values into the provided fields and submit the information using the form.

If you are a representative, you can select the patient for whom you're reporting from the list displayed, allowing you to manage the health data of multiple individuals efficiently.

Upon submission, the system records and stores the data securely, ensuring accurate tracking for remote monitoring purposes.

Any mistakes or incorrect entries, such as non-numeric values, will trigger error messages, allowing you to correct any issues before resubmitting the information.

Through this process, you can ensure that both your own and represented individuals' health metrics are up to date and available for remote health tracking.

WebRoot/auth/patient/calendar.jsp: As a patient using this system, you have access to an appointment calendar where you can view your scheduled appointments, office visits, and lab procedures. You can navigate through months to manage your schedule effectively. The calendar highlights the current day and organizes your healthcare-related activities based on dates. For each day, you can see detailed descriptions of appointments, the type of office visits, and lab procedures, adding convenience to your healthcare management. Clicking on the activity's details provides further information, assisting you in staying informed about your health activities and results. This seamless interaction helps in keeping track of upcoming health-related tasks and efficiently managing your medical requirements.

As a patient using this system, you have the ability to update your personal details through a structured form. This form allows you to input and revise information like your name, address, and contact details. It also includes sections for updating your insurance details and managing your financial information such as credit card type and number. Furthermore, you can enhance your account safety by setting a security question and answer, which will help verify your identity for future transactions. Additionally, it provides a section for you to list an emergency contact, ensuring that your healthcare provider knows who to reach out to in case of a medical emergency. After updating these details to your satisfaction, you submit the form, and should there be any validation issues, you would receive immediate feedback. The system understates that password changes are facilitated separately, guiding you to the login page for password-related adjustments.

WebRoot/auth/patient/home.jsp:
As a patient accessing this system, you would:  
Log into your personalized dashboard to review important health-related information and updates.  
You would receive notifications and reminders about incomplete surveys from your recent office visits, with direct links provided to complete them if needed.  
Check any ongoing or previous report requests to track their status.  
View recent lab procedures performed during the last month, including detailed results, both for yourself and any patients you are authorized to represent.  
Receive alerts about any unauthorized access to your medical records, specifying the personnel responsible and the date of access within the last 90 days.  
This user-friendly system enables you to actively manage your healthcare by ensuring you are aware of and can respond to any incomplete tasks, maintain oversight of your health information, and secure your medical data from undue access.

WebRoot/auth/patient/information.jsp:
As a patient using this system, you would:
Log in to access your personal information.
View your profile details, including your full name, gender, location (city and state), date of birth, and blood type.
See a picture of yourself, personalized with your specific medical identification number (MID).
This system allows you to conveniently review your personal and demographic information which is securely retrieved and displayed.

WebRoot/auth/patient/menu.jsp:
As a patient using this system, you have access to various self-service functionalities conveniently organized under different categories. You can edit personal details such as demographics to ensure your information is up-to-date. The system enables you to view your access log, check your calendar for important dates, review past diagnoses, and see a list of healthcare providers you have visited. To keep track of your medical history, you can view your medical records and prescription details, including any expired prescriptions.

Consult the appointments section to manage your schedule and view upcoming visits to your healthcare providers. For effective communication, use the messaging section to check your inbox and outbox for correspondence with healthcare professionals. If you are enrolled in remote monitoring, report your current health status under telemedicine to keep your care providers informed.

Finally, for additional insights, you may view satisfaction survey results and examine your email history for any communication with the system or your healthcare team. This structured menu empowers you to manage your health-related tasks and communications with ease and transparency.

WebRoot/auth/patient/messageInbox.jsp:
As a patient using this system, you would: 
Access your inbox to view a list of messages, which includes the sender name, subject, and the date received. 
You have the option to sort these messages based on the sender or the time they were received, either in ascending or descending order. 
If you want to filter out messages for easier management, you can customize your message filter criteria by editing the message filter. This allows you to set conditions based on the sender, specific words in the message, message subject, and date range. You can test your filter before applying it to make sure it captures the messages you're interested in.
If you don’t see any messages after filtering, it might be indicative of your filter settings being too restrictive.
Unopened messages are bolded, making it easy for you to spot messages you haven't read yet.
When you click on a message, you will be redirected to read the full content of the message. This system helps you efficiently manage and organize your messages to ensure you don’t miss important communications from your healthcare providers.

WebRoot/auth/patient/messageOutbox.jsp:
As a patient using this system, you would:
- Log into your account to access your outbox, which contains a list of all the messages you have sent.
- View your sent messages, including details like the recipient's name, the message subject, and the date it was sent.
- Sort these messages by the recipient's name or the date sent, in either ascending or descending order, according to your needs.
- Open individual messages to read the content if needed.
- If you wish to send a new message, you have the option to navigate directly to the message composition page.
This system helps you manage and track communications with your healthcare provider by allowing easy access to your sent messages.

WebRoot/auth/patient/myDiagnoses.jsp: As a patient using this medical system, you can access your list of diagnoses. The system presents each diagnosis with a description, which can be clicked to view more information about healthcare professionals (HCPs) who have experience with that specific diagnosis. If you select a diagnosis, you will see a list of HCPs, detailing the number of patients treated for the diagnosis, any prescriptions they have ordered, lab procedures conducted, and satisfaction ratings for office visits and treatments. This helps you to understand your diagnosis better and provides insight into the professionals skilled in managing your condition, potentially assisting you in choosing healthcare providers based on their experience and patient satisfaction.

WebRoot/auth/patient/reply.jsp: As a patient using this system, you have the ability to reply to messages you receive from healthcare providers. When you access the reply page, ensure you have a previous message selected to reply to. The system will retrieve the sender's information and the subject line of the original message, preparing a response draft with a prefixed subject indicating it's a reply. Fill in a new or continued subject if necessary and compose your reply in the textbox provided. Once you have reviewed your message, click the "Send" button to forward the message back to the original sender. If the required elements are missing, the system redirects you to your inbox, guiding you to initiate your reply from there, ensuring efficient communication with your healthcare provider.

As a patient using this system, you would be able to report any adverse reactions or issues encountered with medications. You start by accessing the adverse event reporting form, where you're prompted to describe the adverse event in the provided text area. Once you have filled out the details, submitting the form will send your report about the medication reaction to the relevant healthcare provider. Depending on your access, the system might link your report to the specific healthcare provider or prescription that you had interacted with. This ensures that the medication prescriber is notified about the adverse event, helping them manage the patient's care effectively. This process enables a seamless communication channel between patients and healthcare providers regarding medication safety and efficacy.

WebRoot/auth/patient/sendMessage.jsp: As a patient using this system, you are able to send messages to your healthcare providers (DLHCPs) or send messages on behalf of other patients who have designated you as their representative. To send a message, you first select the intended recipient from the list of your healthcare providers or from the list of healthcare providers of the patient you represent. After selecting your recipient, you compose your message by entering a subject and the message body. Once the message is composed, you submit it to be sent to the recipient. If you have not set up any healthcare providers or have not been designated as a representative by other patients, the system will inform you accordingly. This messaging system facilitates communication between patients and healthcare professionals, ensuring that messages are delivered to the correct individuals efficiently.

WebRoot/auth/patient/showEmailHistory.js: As a patient using this system, you can access a detailed history of your email communications. This feature displays a list of emails that have been sent to you, providing information such as the recipients, subject lines, message contents, and the dates they were sent. You can quickly reference past communications, helping you stay organized and informed about your interactions and any important information you may have received via email. If there have been no emails recorded, the system will inform you that there are currently no emails on record. This helps ensure you have access to your email history in a clear and concise manner.

WebRoot/auth/patient/survey.jsp: As a patient using this system's survey function, you would complete a feedback form following your office visit. Firstly, you will enter the length of time you spent in the waiting room and examination room during the visit. This helps the healthcare provider assess efficiency in process flow and patient throughput. Next, you are invited to rate your satisfaction with the visit and the treatment or information received using a scale from 1 (very unhappy) to 5 (very satisfied). Once you submit your responses, the survey data will be stored and associated with the specific office visit you had. This enables healthcare providers to evaluate service quality and make improvements based on patient experiences, ultimately enhancing patient care and satisfaction in future visits.

WebRoot/auth/patient/viewAccessLog.jsp: As a patient using this system, you would be able to view a log of who has accessed your health information. You would begin by specifying a date range to filter the access records, allowing you to narrow down the time period you are interested in reviewing. Once the date range is set, you can see a list of all personnel or any representatives who have accessed your records within that period. Each entry in the log will show you the date of access, the name of the person who accessed your information, their role, and a description of the access. You have the option to sort the access entries either by date or by the role of the accessor. If you find any unauthorized access, you can take it up with the concerned authorities for further investigation. This tool helps keep track of your data privacy and ensures transparency in who accesses your health information.

WebRoot/auth/patient/viewAppt.jsp: As a patient using this system, you would first select an appointment from a list of your scheduled appointments. Upon choosing an appointment, you will be presented with detailed information about that appointment. This includes the healthcare provider assigned to the appointment, the type of appointment, the scheduled date and time, and the expected duration. If there are any comments associated with the appointment, those will also be displayed. The system ensures that you can easily view all necessary details for your upcoming appointments, helping you manage your healthcare interactions effectively. If you ever encounter an issue, like selecting an appointment that doesn't exist, the system will redirect you to a relevant page to guide you back on track.

WebRoot/auth/patient/viewExpiredPrescrip: As a patient using this system, you would: Access your expired prescription records through your account. You will see a list of all prescriptions that have passed their effective duration, with details including the medication code, description, the period the prescription was active, and the name of the healthcare provider who prescribed it. If no expired prescriptions are found, you will be notified that there are no records. You can click on each prescription to view more detailed information regarding that medication if needed. This function allows you to easily keep track of your medication history and provides contact information for healthcare professionals associated with each prescription.

WebRoot/auth/patient/viewLabProc.jsp:
As a patient using this system, you would:
Log in to view your laboratory procedures ordered by your healthcare provider. 
You can see detailed information about each lab procedure, including its lab code, current status, any commentary provided by the healthcare professionals, the results, the related office visit ID, and when the procedure was last updated. 
If you do not select a specific procedure ID from your list, you'll be redirected to your calendar view where you can schedule or view appointments. 
This system allows you to efficiently track your lab results and stay informed on your healthcare journey.

WebRoot/auth/patient/viewLHCP.jsp:
As a patient using this system, you would:

View detailed information about a specific health care provider (LHCP) that you have visited. This would include the provider's full name, specialty, contact details, and address.

To access the information, you would typically select the LHCP from a list of providers you have visited. After selection, the system would present you with the LHCP’s profile, allowing you to see:
- Their specialty, such as cardiology, pediatrics, or general practice.
- Their physical address, including street, city, state, and zip code, which might help you when planning your visit.
- Their phone number, enabling you to make direct contact if needed, except when it's presented as unavailable.
- Their email address for inquiries or communication about appointments or follow-ups.

This interface gives you the necessary information to manage your interactions with health care providers effectively, ensuring you have all the necessary details at your fingertips for communication or further consultation.

WebRoot/auth/patient/viewMessageInbox.js: As a patient using this system, you would access your message inbox to view messages sent to you by healthcare professionals or administrative staff. When selecting a specific message, the system retrieves that communication's details, including the sender's name, subject, and the date and time it was sent. You'll be able to read the message in full and have an option to reply directly through the system's interface. This feature ensures efficient communication between you and your healthcare providers, allowing for fast and organized exchanges of information.

WebRoot/auth/patient/viewMessageOutbox.j: As a patient using this system, you can view the details of a message you have sent. You will select a message from your outbox and the system will display the recipient, subject, date, and time it was sent, along with the message content.
